newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish troops said to kill over 30 rebel Kurds.
newsitem.headline: Turkish troops said to kill over 30 rebel Kurds.

text.p: Turkish troops have killed more than 30 separatist Kurds in fighting in northern Iraq during a two-day-old assault against the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), the state-run Anatolian news agency said on Thursday.
Several thousand heavily armed Turkish troops, backed by air power, poured into northern Iraq on Wednesday in a bid to crush the PKK in the region.

Anatolian said troops had inflicted their first casualties in clashes in what it identified as the Sarisavaklar region across the border from the Turkish province of Sirnak. It said fighting was continuing and the toll was expected to rise.
The agency said F-4 jets from two southeastern Turkish bases had bombed five PKK camps in northern Iraq early on Thursday. U.S.-made Cobra helicopters continued the assault on the camps.

Iraqi Kurdish peshmerga guerrillas of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) were involved in fierce clashes with the PKK in the Begova and Derkar areas northeast of Zakho, the main town in the area, Anatolian said.
Turkey's defence minister has said KDP leader Massoud Barzani invited troops in, but the KDP has declined to comment on its role in the operation so far.
Anatolian said Turkish troops had also begun a big assault around the mountains to the west of the region, towards Iraq's borders with Syria.
